newsitem.title: UK: British jazz musician died of overdose - coroner.
newsitem.headline: British jazz musician died of overdose - coroner.

text.p: Ronnie Scott, the saxophonist whose London club became a mecca for jazz musicians, died of a drugs overdose, a British coroner ruled on Wednesday.
Scott was found dead at his London home on December 23, aged 69, and there were widespread reports he had committed suicide because of depression.
Coroner Paul Knapman recorded a verdict of misadventure, saying "an incautious overdose of barbiturates" had led to Scott's death.
The drugs which led to Scott's death were prescribed by his dentist who was conducting extensive treatment on the musician.
Scott founded the club bearing his name in Soho in 1959, and a roll-call of the stars that played there included Dizzy Gillespie, Sarah Vaughan, Django Reinhardt and Jimi Hendrix.
Scott, known for his irreverent sense of humour and for dressing all in black, started playing at the age of 13.

A self-effacing man who never married, Scott was inspired to open his club after discovering the jazz scene in New York after World War Two. Regular customers in the 1960s and 1970s included the Rolling Stones, the Beatles and Rod Stewart.
